title: Batcher Odyssey: workload inspector and continuous parameter advisor
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem statement: Many Redwood workloads show intermittent token-level cost spikes and poor GPU utilization because batching parameters (microbatch size, max coalescing window, KV-windowing) are hand-tuned per team and drift with traffic patterns. Current recommendations are static heuristics or one-off profiling runs; we need a continuously running inspector that produces conservative recommendations and an automated, safe apply/rollback workflow integrated with Console and Redwood Optimize.

Goal: Build Batcher Odyssey — a workload inspector + continuous parameter advisor that: 1) profiles request arrival patterns, sequence length distributions, and KV cache reuse across namespaces and model variants; 2) synthesizes conservative, workload-aware batching/caching parameter suggestions (microbatch target, coalescing latency budget, prefix-KV retention, affinity tags); 3) automatically stages changes via canary policies, monitors production signals, and rolls back safely on regressions.

Core components: 
- Data ingestor: streaming telemetry consumer reading request traces (model, route, tokens, latency, KV hit/miss, queue times) from tracing pipeline and Custom Metrics (Console).
- Profile synthesizer: incremental sketching (time-windowed histograms + sketch of sequence length percentiles, inter-arrival CDF) that creates a compact workload fingerprint.
- Heuristic engine: rule-based scoring layer that maps fingerprints to parameter candidates. Rules include cost-estimate delta, latency SLO risk, KV-safety (do not reduce KV retention below observed reuse half-life), and burst-sensitivity adjustments.
- Continuous tuner: lightweight optimizer that proposes a single conservative delta from baseline (e.g., increase microbatch by +15% or increase coalescing window by +8ms) with shadow simulation on traffic samples.
- Safe apply orchestrator: automated canary rollout in 3 stages (shadow evaluate, 5% canary, 30% ramp) with automated rollback triggers wired to signal checks in Console.

Decision trade-offs and constraints: 
- Conservative vs aggressive: initial product must prefer under-tuning (missed cost savings) over user-visible latency regressions. We use a tunable risk parameter per customer tier.
- Telemetry fidelity: To operate in private deployments we only rely on summary telemetry (sketches + counts) to avoid PII transfer.
- Simulation cost: Shadow simulation should be cheap; we evaluate on sampled traces rather than full-replay.

Success criteria: 
- Automatic recommendations accepted by users for >=20% of profiled routes within 8 weeks of rollout.
- No rollbacks triggered by more than 0.2% of automated applies after stabilization period.
- Aggregate per-token cost reduction >=6% for routes that accept suggestions.

Integration touchpoints: 
- Console: new Recommendations tab per route; actions: preview, stage canary, apply, rollback.
- Redwood Optimize: show cost delta and suggested quantization pairing when relevant.
- API: /v1/admin/batching/recommendations endpoints for fetch/ack/apply.

Open questions: 
- Should we expose a global safety budget (tolerable P99 increase) or per-route SLO budget? (initial design uses per-route with tenant-global cap).
- How to handle workloads where KV reuse is sparse but microbatching still beneficial? Proposed: prefer coalescing adjustments over KV retention cuts; require explicit opt-in for KV retention changes.

Timeline and milestones: 
1) Week 0-2: Set up telemetry sketches and profile synthesizer prototype; validate on sample production traces.
2) Week 2-5: Implement heuristic engine & cost estimator; run offline candidate generation and simulation.
3) Week 5-8: Build safe apply orchestrator and integrate Console actions; implement rollback monitors.
4) Week 8-12: Canary rollout with internal accounts and early adopter customers; tune risk parameters.

Rollout plan and rollback playbook: 
- Staging: shadow-evaluate recommendations for 48 hours against golden metrics.
- Canary: 5% traffic for 24 hours; check latency P50/P95/P99, error rate, and user-defined SLOs every 5 minutes.
- Ramp: 30% for 48 hours, then full apply if stable.
- Automated rollback triggers: P99 latency increase > configuration threshold, error rate spike > 0.5% above baseline, KV miss rate increase leading to >2% cost delta.
- Manual review gates for any apply that touches KV retention or model routing.

Observability and telemetry: 
- New Console dashboard panels: profile heatmaps (sequence length vs request rate), proposed parameter delta, predicted cost delta, and safety score.
- Alerting: automated alerts to SRE on first rollback or repeated flaky suggestions.

Data privacy and safety: 
- Only ingest aggregate sketches and percentiles for Private deployments; for hosted we may use richer traces under customer consent.
- All proposals are reversible; any apply produces a stamped checkpoint in config history with fast rollback path.

Implementation notes and choices: 
- Use time-windowed t-digests for sequence-length percentiles and Count-Min sketches for route counting to keep payloads compact.
- Cost estimator: tokenized cost model + throughput multiplier; simulate batching effects by modeling queueing delay under Poisson arrivals approximated by measured inter-arrival distribution.
- Heuristics: prioritize microbatch increases when median sequence > 32 tokens and tail variance low; prioritize coalescing when inter-arrival 95th percentile < coalescing window target.

Deliverables: 
- Prototype profile synthesizer (service + feature flag), offline recommendation runner, canary orchestrator, Console UI mockups, integration tests, and runbook.

Longer-term: integrate ML-based candidate ranker, multi-parameter optimizer (jointly tune microbatch and coalescing), and per-customer risk profiles.

References: Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/Batcher+Odyssey, Design mockups: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/example-batcher-odyssey, Telemetry dashboard: https://console.redwood.internal/dashboards/batcher-odyssey
